name: uMonitor
request:
I would like to have an app for windows that allows to prepare a cockpit to monitor various data and show it on the connected screen (480x320 pixels) in landscape or portrait mode. 
The app should allow for designing a layout with:
- choice of landscape or portrait
- a wall paper chosen from filesystem, that should be resized to the screen resolution,
- place with drag and drop predefined fields, like the ones in the example app, but also add other data like 
    - text strings
	- stock tickers, 
    - weather info, 
    - status of homeassistant provided data (configure homeassistant address and drag and drop data)
    - json sources retrieved via http or https (to provide address and drag and drop fields)
    - other you suggest
These data fields and indicators should be possible to place freely on the screen, but there is also an option to activate a grid to snap controls. 
To display data it should also support 
- pie chart, 
- data bars, 
- all the other features provided in the example app. 
The application should have a front end for creating a new design, load from disk (both the old format and in new json format), modify it, save it (both in the old format and in the new format in json format), upload it to the screen, etc.
When minimized it should run in the windows tray. By clicking the tray icon it should maximize the window. by right clicking it should present the option to:
- open the app (maximize the window)
- add/remove to windows startup
- exit

The original is a .NET program, and its obfuscated names don’t appear in the native string search. I’ve opened it in Deep mode and am following its managed references alongside the requested pseudocode calls to recover usable rules.
I found a saved arc setting the importer was dropping: the original can leave a gap at every fourth 3.6° segment. I’m tracing that setting through the drawing and transfer functions, then I’ll preserve it in imported dashboards and verify the rendered result.
All 48 requested function reads are complete and saved with their matching .NET instructions and references. The new tests reproduced the dropped arc setting; after the fix, both import and rendering tests pass. I’m updating the mechanics sheet and checking the full build and portable ZIP.
The release build and all 56 tests pass. Craft’s startup and mechanics checks also pass, and the rebuilt portable ZIP passes its file and checksum checks. I’m now checking the packaged app and visually reviewing the recovered arc gaps.
